title: Distribution-Table Approximation for Neural Distinguisher Block 2-i
summary: On SPECK-32/64, the proposed approximation closely matches the neural distinguisher’s accuracy and predictions, but whether it captures Block 2-i’s internal processing remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the neural distinguisher's internal data processing of residual Block 2-i, determine whether the processing can be approximated by computing a distribution table for each input $I=(\Delta L,\Delta V,V_0,V_1)$, where the associated probabilities $P(\text{Real}\mid I_M)$ for all masks $M\in R_M$ are concatenated into a feature vector of size $m=|R_M|$.

scope.domain: Machine-learning-based symmetric cryptanalysis using a masked distribution-table representation of a neural distinguisher’s residual block.
parameters: I = (ΔL, ΔV, V₀, V₁): input to the proposed distribution table
m = |R_M|: number of mask-conditioned probabilities and feature-vector size
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish whether the concatenated mask-conditioned distribution-table probabilities approximate the internal processing of residual Block 2-i.

citations.label: A Deeper Look at Machine Learning-Based Cryptanalysis

progress.summary: The paper states this explicitly as Conjecture 5 and tests the proposed approximation on SPECK-32/64, reporting close accuracy and prediction matching. Mask extraction still relies on the DNN, and eliminating that reliance is left as future work.
citation_labels: Adrien Benamira et al., A Deeper Look at Machine Learning-Based Cryptanalysis
